title: Day of the Week
statement:
A calendar date (in the Gregorian calendar) arrives as three integers: `day` of the month, `month` (1 for January through 12 for December) and `year`. Return the weekday it falls on, spelled exactly as one of `"Sunday"`, `"Monday"`, `"Tuesday"`, `"Wednesday"`, `"Thursday"`, `"Friday"` or `"Saturday"`.

As a reference point, 1 January 1971 was a Friday. Every input is a real date from a year between 1971 and 2100 inclusive.
constraints: day is a valid day of that month in that year (leap years included)
signature: String dayOfTheWeek(int day, int month, int year)
notes:
## Intuition

Weekdays repeat every 7 days, so if we know how many days separate the given date from a date whose weekday is known, the remainder mod 7 tells us the answer. The statement hands us that anchor: 1 January 1971 was a Friday. All that remains is counting days carefully, which mostly means getting leap years right.

## Approach

1. Keep `names` in Sunday-first order, so Friday sits at index 5, and `monthDays` for a common year.
2. Add 366 to `days` for each leap year from 1971 up to (not including) `year`, and 365 for each other year.
3. Add the lengths of the full months before `month`.
4. If the date is after February in a leap year, add the extra day for 29 February.
5. Add `day - 1` for the days already passed in the current month.
6. Return `names[(days + 5) % 7]`: shifting by 5 maps zero elapsed days to Friday.

## Example 1, step by step

For 31 August 2019: the 48 years 1971–2018 include 12 leap years, giving `48 · 365 + 12 = 17532`. January to July 2019 add `212`, and 2019 is not a leap year. Then `day - 1 = 30`, so `days = 17774`. Finally `(17774 + 5) % 7 = 6`, which is `"Saturday"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(1): at most 130 years and 11 months are summed.
- Space: O(1).

## Pitfalls

- Century years are leap only when divisible by 400: 2000 is leap, 2100 is not.
- The extra leap day matters only for dates after February of that same year.
- Count elapsed days (`day - 1`), not the day number itself, or every answer shifts by one.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `names` | weekday names, Sunday first |
| `monthDays` | lengths of the months in a common year |
| `isLeap` | Gregorian leap-year test |
| `days` | days elapsed since 1 January 1971 |
| `y`, `m` | loop counters over whole years and whole months |

narration.2: Weekday names in Sunday-first order, so Friday is at index 5.
narration.3: Month lengths for a year without 29 February.
narration.4: A year is leap if divisible by 4, except centuries that are not divisible by 400.
narration.6: Count the days elapsed since 1 January 1971.
narration.7: Walk over every whole year before the given one...
narration.8: ...adding 366 days for a leap year and 365 otherwise.
narration.10: Then walk over the whole months before the given month...
narration.13: Past February in a leap year means 29 February has already happened.
narration.16: Add the days already gone in the current month.
narration.17: Zero elapsed days is a Friday (index 5), so shift by 5 and wrap around the week.
